speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: The SkillsFuture Credit is one part of the SkillsFuture movement to empower individuals to take ownership of their skills development and lifelong learning journey.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: So, while training programmes offered by the Continuing Education and Training (CET) Centres and PSEIs are developed in close collaboration with industries with a strong focus on employment outcomes, the SkillsFuture Credit covers a much larger range of courses because part of its purpose is also to raise awareness of the importance of lifelong learning and skills mastery.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: However, that is part of the outcome of the empowerment of individuals and their holistic development.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I took a look at the SkillsFuture portal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Of the top eight most popular courses, six deal with health and fitness, baking, Korean language, sewing and photography.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They appear to be courses for the pursuit of hobbies, even though they can be counted as part of lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: My question in the Parliamentary Question is more that, given that Government monies are being used for SkillsFuture Credit, can more be done to ensure that the courses being provided are ultimately bound to our pursuit of economic value-add for society?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to reassure her and Members that when approving SkillsFuture Credit courses, we take into careful consideration whether it is skills-based and relevant to industry needs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: There are more than 50 areas of training and we will stop at the top 10.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Sharing the list is to assure Members that when we select these courses, together in partnership with the supporting public agencies, we look closely at whether it is skills-based and whether it is relevant to industry.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That being said, earlier, I mentioned that SkillsFuture Credit courses also serve to empower Singaporeans in their lifelong learning journey and holistic development.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Singaporeans are able to opt for approved courses that are not directly related to their vocations or careers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But they are perhaps learning it as they are planning to move into adjacent growth areas or they are learning it because they would like to whet their appetite before they start up their own bakery shop, for example.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Ms Sun Xueling and Members that as part of the evaluation process, we look at industry relevance, and SkillsFuture Credit eligible courses also undergo an industry validation process.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As I had mentioned earlier, courses under the WSQ framework are pegged to industry needs and standards.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: SSG involves industry representatives who identify the skill needs in the respective sector and validate the skill standards.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I was thinking that, specifically for some courses that have a particular pertinence given the Committee on the Future Economy's recommendations, can more be done to subsidise such courses beyond the $500 SkillsFuture Credit?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The $500 Credit can be used, on top of the course fee subsidies provided by the Government.
